title: Caching and Response Efficiency
subtopics: Avoiding caching sensitive or user-specific responses incorrectly
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of caching and response efficiency in a Classic ASP application.
Identify and describe at least two syllabus subtopics: Cache fundamentals and Browser caching headers.
Inspect a minimal example and define a reproducible normal-case and failure-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study caching and response efficiency as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 104 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: Caching and Response Efficiency matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Production readiness means controlled configuration, limited privileges, measured performance, resource cleanup, repeatable deployment, and recoverable backups. For 'Caching and Response Efficiency', record the exact IIS and OS assumptions, test the plan in a non-production environment, and define verification plus rollback criteria before changing live settings.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: Cache fundamentals; Browser caching headers; Response expiration settings; Caching static assets; Caching appropriate read-only data; Cache invalidation; Avoiding caching sensitive or user-specific responses incorrectly. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Caching and Response Efficiency
content_blocks.code:
<%
Response.Buffer = True
Response.ContentType = "text/html"
' Render the complete response before sending when the page is of manageable size.
%>
content_blocks.expected_output: Response buffering is enabled for the page.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Avoid repeated flushing and unbounded output. Cache only data that is safe to reuse; invalidate when the underlying data changes. The standard CodeLeaf browser playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only; it does not execute Classic ASP, VBScript, ADO, IIS commands, PowerShell, or SQL. This block is therefore marked for static inspection unless you run it in the clearly identified local tool.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original sample and test data. Change one condition, input, provider setting, or runtime option at a time, then compare observed behavior with the expected result.
content_blocks.limitations: Not executed during course generation. Classic ASP examples require a configured Windows/IIS environment with the matching ASP scripting engine and any required COM/ADO providers. Provider-specific and IIS-version-specific behavior must be verified locally.

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Use a staging environment, written acceptance criteria, version-controlled changes, and a rollback plan. Record evidence instead of claiming a deployment or migration was tested if it was not. The source syllabus treats Classic ASP as a legacy maintenance technology, not as ASP.NET or a default choice for new web projects.

content_blocks.title: Guided workflow
content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of caching and response efficiency. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small, reviewable demonstration of caching and response efficiency using synthetic data. Include at least one of these syllabus concepts: Cache fundamentals. State the expected result first, then add one invalid or boundary case and explain how your program should behave.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming syntax alone proves the application works.
common_mistakes.why: IIS configuration, permissions, COM activation, database providers, and response behavior are external dependencies.
common_mistakes.fix: Run against the documented local test host and record exact evidence.

common_mistakes.why: Query strings, form fields, cookies, and hidden controls remain client-controlled.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate on the server and apply authorization and output encoding at the appropriate boundary.
